items.understanding: The stock holds its ground and its RS rating rises to 87 because institutions are quietly supporting its price and refusing to let it drop.
items.cause: Institutions quietly supporting the price and refusing to let it fall
items.effect: The stock holds its ground and its RS rating is pushed up to 87
items.asserted: Institutions are quietly supporting the stock's price, refusing to let it fall, which holds its ground and pushes its RS rating up to 87.

notAsserted.text: The stock price is falling freely
notAsserted.why: The narration explicitly states institutions refuse to let it fall and it is holding its ground.

notAsserted.text: Institutions are aggressively and publicly bidding up the stock
notAsserted.why: The narration states support is occurring quietly.

keyFacts: The stock's RS rating is pushed up to 87.
The stock is holding its ground.
Institutions are quietly supporting the price.
Institutions refuse to let the stock fall.
wrong: A high RS rating of 87 causes institutions to quietly begin supporting the stock price.
The stock is dropping sharply because institutions refuse to support it.
Quiet institutional selling is holding the stock's ground and lowering its RS rating.

items.understanding: Riding out a severe bear market cuts your capital base in half and destroys the magic of compound interest according to O'Neil's math.
items.cause: Riding out a severe bear market and having your capital base cut in half
items.effect: The magic of compound interest is destroyed
items.asserted: Your capital base is cut in half, and O'Neil's math proves that riding out a severe bear market destroys the magic of compound interest.

notAsserted.text: Holding through a bear market preserves compound interest
notAsserted.why: The narration asserts that writing out a severe bear market destroys compound interest.

notAsserted.text: Compound interest continues without capital loss
notAsserted.why: The narration states that the capital base is cut in half.

keyFacts: The capital base is cut in half.
O'Neil has mathematical proof regarding bear markets.
Writing out a severe bear market destroys the magic of compound interest.
wrong: The destruction of compound interest causes an investor's capital base to be cut in half.
O'Neil's math proves that enduring a severe bear market strengthens compound interest.
Cutting your capital base in half accelerates the power of compound interest.
